answer: Under clique-entropy ink tests, each new identity joining the tundra network must submit a puzzle solution whose difficulty scales with sibling joins sharing any 64-bit hardware or behavioral sketch in the past 24 hours, so the k-th clone pays k times full work: ten clones cost 55 units versus ten for honest agents, a nonlinear wall pushing attacker cost past its nadir only when clusters grow.
